Expert comments next to their ratings

Source: R/comments.R
delphi_comments.Rd

Lists the comments of the experts with the rating that their author gave to the same item in the same round, on every indicator, and the position of that rating relative to the ratings of the whole panel: below the first quartile, within the interquartile range or above the third quartile. Comments from experts whose ratings lie outside the interquartile range are the arguments of the minority, which the Delphi method asks the panel to consider in the next round.

Usage

delphi_comments(x, round = NULL, items = NULL, general = TRUE, type = 7)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object with comments; see delphi_add_comments().

round, items

Optional subsets of rounds and items.

general

Whether to include general comments, not referring to a specific item.

type

Quantile algorithm; see delphi_describe().

Value

A data frame of class delphi_comments with one row per comment and columns round, item, expert, indicator, comment, theme, then, for each indicator, the rating of the author (<indicator>_rating) and its position (<indicator>_position), and finally outside_iqr: whether the rating of the author lies outside the interquartile range on at least one indicator.

Details

A rating equal to a quartile counts as within the interquartile range. Positions are NA for general comments and when the author did not rate the item on that indicator.

See also

delphi_comment_counts(), delphi_themes(), delphi_words(), delphi_feedback().

Examples

r1 <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
                 E1 = c(7, 8, 6, 2), E2 = c(3, 5, 4, 9))
x <- delphi_data(r1, expert_col = "expert", indicator = "impact")
cm <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "D"), item = c("E1", "E1"),
                 comment = c("Depends on public funding.",
                             "Unlikely without new regulation."))
x <- delphi_add_comments(x, cm)
delphi_comments(x)
#> <delphi_comments> 2 comment(s)
#> 
#> Round 1, item E1
#>   [A]: impact within IQR
#>     Depends on public funding.
#>   [D]: impact below Q1
#>     Unlikely without new regulation.
